text.en: A lahar is essentially the same thing as a lava flow, just given a different name -- both are just 'volcanic material flowing downhill' -- in reality, a lahar is a mudflow of volcanic ash/debris mixed with water (from rain, melted snow/ice, or a crater lake), mechanistically distinct from molten lava, and lahars can occur long after an eruption has ended (whenever water mixes with loose volcanic debris on the slopes), not only during active eruption.
text.et: Lahar on sisuliselt sama asi kui laavavoog, lihtsalt teise nimega -- mõlemad on lihtsalt 'vulkaaniline materjal, mis voolab allamäge' -- tegelikult on lahar vulkaanilise tuha/rusu mudavoog, mis on segunenud veega (vihmast, sulanud lumest/jääst või kraatrijärvest), mehaaniliselt eristuv sulanud laavast, ning lahareid võib esineda kaua pärast purske lõppu (alati, kui vesi seguneb lahtise vulkaanilise rusuga nõlvadel), mitte ainult aktiivse purske ajal.
